name_en: Nankan-age makizushi — sushi rolled in sweet-simmered fried tofu skin instead of nori
summary_ja: 海苔の代わりに、甘辛く煮た薄い油揚げ「南関あげ」で酢飯と具材を巻いた寿司。南関あげは二度揚げして水分を抜いた保存性の高い油揚げで、出汁がよく出ることから汁物にも重宝されるという。
summary_en: Vinegared rice and fillings are rolled not in nori but in nankan-age, a thin fried tofu skin simmered sweet and salty. Twice-fried to remove moisture for long keeping, nankan-age is also prized for the rich broth it releases in soups.
source_title: 南関あげ巻き寿司 熊本県

name_en: Konoshiro no sugatazushi — whole vinegar-cured konoshiro stuffed with sushi rice
summary_ja: 背開きにしたコノシロを甘酢で締め、腹に棒状の酢飯を詰めて頭と尾を立てて盛る祝い寿司。八代海沿岸に江戸時代から伝わるとされ、鮮度が落ちやすいコノシロを酢で締めて日持ちさせる知恵という。
summary_en: Konoshiro herring, split along the back and cured in sweet vinegar, is stuffed with a log of sushi rice and plated head and tail upright — a festive sushi said to date to the Edo period along the Yatsushiro Sea, the vinegar cure a way to keep fast-spoiling fish.
source_title: このしろの姿寿司 熊本県
